references.text: Describes the slaughter of a bull as a burnt offering at the entrance to the tent of meeting, before the Lord's presence - the same location and procedure as in Exodus 29:11
The bull is to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the Lord's presence, where it shall be slaughtered - identical wording and ritual practice
Moses slaughtered the bull at the consecration of Aaron and his sons - fulfilling the instruction given in Exodus 29:11
Slaughter at the entrance to the tent of meeting as part of the peace offering ritual
The command that all slaughter offerings must be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the Lord
The altar of burnt offering was placed at the entrance to the tabernacle, the place where the slaughter was to take place
Christ entered the holy place with his own blood, once for all - fulfilling the Old Testament sacrificial rituals
A theological parallel showing that the laying on of hands during slaughter applies to both priests and the congregation.
